BME 100: First-year seminar to introduce the students to the field of biomedical engineering, and related opportunities in research, and industry.
BME 201: Cell and molecular biology taught from an engineering perspective.
BME 301: Analysis of physiological signals and modeling of physiological systems by electrical and mechanical analogs in the context of continuous linear systems.
BME 303: Mechanical properties of fluids and solids with applications to tissue mechanics and vascular system.
BME 313: Chemical processes, including material and energy balances and heat transfer with emphasis on biological and biomedical applications.
BME 399: Courses offered in foreign countries by individual or group instruction.
BME 401: Integration of design theory and finite element analyses for the development of solutions to problems in biomedical engineering.
BME 402: Biomedical measurements, including consideration of techniques, equipment, and safety.
BME 403: Building basic biomedical signal processing circuits and biomedical measurement systems, experiments in medical imaging techniques, and measurement of bio-potentials.
BME 406: Physical principles and clinical applications of medical imaging methods.
BME 408: This course presents advanced topics in solid mechanics that are important for understanding the behavior and function of biological materials, including cardiovascular tissues (e.g., blood vessels, myocardium, epicardium), musculoskeletal tissues (e.g., tendon, bone, articular cartilage), synthetic biomaterials (e.g., hydrogels, composites), and cells.
BME 409: The fundamental relations in fluid mechanics and their application to biofluids including steady/unsteady flows, diseased states, devices and biorheology.
BME 410: Study of fluid mechanics at small length scales including fabrication of microfluidic devices and microfluidic components, lab-on-chip concept and applications.
BME 413: An integrated study of the fundamentals of mass transport processes with emphasis on the analysis of physiological systems.
BME 419: Analysis of function and consideration of design concerns for biomedical implants, including prosthetic joints, electrical stimulators, and cardiovascular pumps.
BME 423: Chemical kinetics and reaction equilibria with applications to the analysis of physiological function and the design of synthetic organs.
BME 429: Experimental laboratory that includes hands-on measurement, computational simulations, and statistical analysis of biofluids, biosolids, and biomaterial phenomena.
BME 433: Engineering and biological principles as applied to pharmaceutical transport and designing drug carriers.
BME 437: This course is an introduction to the theory and practice of biomedical data science.
BME 440: Seminar giving students exposure to professionals who apply engineering and related fields to biology and medicine.
BME 443: Describe properties of materials and composites and their in vivo interactions.
BME 444: Focus is on special properties of surface as an important causative and mediating agent in the biological response to materials.
BME 445: Introduction to interdisciplinary tissue engineering concepts, associated biochemical and biomechanical engineering calculations, and cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and other tissue application examples.
BME 446: Foundations in polymer chemistry and physics, polymer design, characterization, and processing with a focus on biomedical applications.
BME 448: This course provides an overview of the FDA regulatory process for drug, biologics, and device development.
BME 450W: Team based capstone design course with open ended project for industry or clinical applications related to Biomedical Engineering.
BME 455: This course will give an overview of milestones in stem cell research and will expose students to current topics at the frontier of this field.
BME 494H: Independent study research and design, leading towards honors thesis.
BME 496: Creative projects, including research and design, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
BME 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject which may be topical or of special interest.
BME 499: Courses offered in foreign countries by individual or group instruction.
